summary: The Hub Audience and the Hub environment are now explicit validated configuration on hub-sdk 1.3.1. A vendored 2.1.0 config validator lands at apps/api/src/config/hub-config.ts; auth-provider.ts is rewritten around hubEnvBag / hubConfigPresence / loadHubAuthConfig / tryLoadHubAuthConfig with NO blanket try/catch, so a bad Hub configuration is a boot failure and only the absent and incomplete presences fail soft into the existing 503. parseAudienceFromPublishableKey is deleted, coreModuleFromAudience keeps working through a widened prefix strip, env.ts drops FXL_HUB_PUBLISHABLE_KEY / FXL_HUB_SECRET_KEY and gains the five new keys, and raw process.env has left app-auth.ts entirely. The SDK was NOT bumped and nothing was installed.

commits.subject: test(api): pin explicit Hub config, offline environment agreement and no NODE_ENV inference
feat(api): make the Hub audience and environment explicit validated configuration
docs(api): retire the Hub publishable and secret key variables

oracles_written.title: accepts a single FXL_HUB_CONFIG JSON object as this repo's documented form
accepts the five discrete variables when FXL_HUB_CONFIG is absent
trims trailing slashes off apiUrl
refuses a plain http apiUrl outside development
refuses a product. audience at boot and names the audience field
refuses an audience that is not app. plus the client id slug
refuses an environment that disagrees with the client id segment, and reaches no network
never consults NODE_ENV to decide the environment
refuses a client secret whose slug or environment disagrees with the client id
refuses FXL_HUB_CONFIG that is not valid JSON
never puts the client secret in an error message or a log line
parses pk_<slug>_<environment>_<random> and keeps underscores inside the random segment
returns null for a key with no environment segment
does not read NODE_ENV anywhere in the Hub config module
loads the Hub contract for app.fxl-sales from FXL_HUB_CONFIG
loads the same contract from the five discrete variables
returns null from the optional loader when no Hub configuration is present at all
returns null from the optional loader when the discrete form is incomplete
refuses an incomplete Hub configuration from the strict loader and names the client secret field
refuses to boot when FXL_HUB_CONFIG is set beside a discrete variable and names every offender
refuses to boot on a product. audience rather than answering 503
requires FXL_HUB_HEALTH_TOKEN outside development
does not require FXL_HUB_HEALTH_TOKEN in development
projects exactly the Hub variables off the validated env object
no API module derives the Hub audience from a key
never leaks the client secret out of the optional loader
resolves the redirect to this app's own origin, never the Hub's
keeps the redirect on this app origin when the Hub api url and the web origin differ
points the BFF callback at this app's own origin rather than the Hub's

no_blanket_catch_proof: grep -n 'try\b|catch' apps/api/src/config/auth-provider.ts returns exactly one line, the header comment on line 9 explaining why there is none; there is no try or catch keyword anywhere in the file body.
deviations_from_plan: app-auth.test.ts: the FXL_HUB_CONFIG blank stub is placed in a vi.hoisted() block rather than the beforeAll the plan names. That file imports ../app-auth.js with a STATIC import, which ESM evaluates before any beforeAll runs, so a beforeAll stub would be a no-op against the module-scope throw it exists to prevent. vi.hoisted runs before the imports and achieves exactly the stated purpose. No existing assertion or title in that file changed.
concerns: The committed publishable-key literal pk_fxl-sales_VzQ9-LUONCnlKllxCRLffN3nw6Z9PQl2 now appears only in apps/web/.env.example, apps/web/.env.dev.example and README.md lines 7 and 24 prose, all of which the plan explicitly leaves to slice 04. It is also present, deliberately, as the negative fixture in the plan's named test 'returns null for a key with no environment segment'.

For one wave CLAUDE.md documents FXL_HUB_PUBLISHABLE_KEY / FXL_HUB_SECRET_KEY, which the API has stopped reading. This is the deliberate consequence of decision D5, and slice 03 carries the correcting bullet verbatim in wave 2.
healthToken is validated and carried on HubAuthConfig but is not yet handed to createHubBff, because the 1.3.1 SDK has no such option. A comment in auth-provider.ts says so; slice 04 wires it.
